doc.title: Ben Sidran interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 15, 2023

title: Record companies in the wild west days
summary: Labels threw money at attitude until real businessmen arrived and genres were divided by the mid-70s.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: Were the members of that band — didn’t deserve to be there really?

One of them had talent, the other three did not deserve to be there. They got signed — you know back then the record companies really had no idea what to do and so they were just throwing money at young people who came through the door with a lot of attitude. And maybe there’d be a kid with a good voice, and maybe they had one song that was kind of catchy. And okay you’ve got a record deal. So it got sorted out of course. As soon as the real money showed up. When the real money showed up the real businessmen showed up, and then it wasn’t a free-for-all anymore. By the mid ‘70s on the one hand you had disco and on the other hand you had heavy metal and on the — you know once it got divided into categories we can sell then we had a business. But up until then it was the wild west.
